summary: The note surveys service learning and community-based projects (CBPs) in education, tracing their roots to John Dewey and the experiential education of the 1960s-70s. It presents examples from 2023-2024 across US cities, plus Project Future and the Global Classroom with Kenya. It also covers challenges such as maintaining academic quality and equitable access, and the role of technology and reflection.
one_line: Overview of service learning and community-based projects in education, covering history, 2023-2024 examples, challenges like equity and quality, and the role of technology.
key_facts: Service learning traces to the early 20th century, when progressive theorist John Dewey advocated connecting education to real-life situations.
In the 1960s and 1970s, the rise of experiential education brought service learning to the forefront in the United States.

In September 2023, educational reformer Dr. Emily Carter led the launch of the "Community Connect" program in Portland, Oregon, where high school students collaborate with local nonprofits on homelessness, environmental conservation, and elderly care.
Community-based projects (CBPs) are typically longer-term endeavors in which students work closely with community members to address a local problem or need.
In October 2023, Detroit high school teacher Michael Anderson spearheaded a community garden project teaching biology and environmental science while addressing neighborhood food scarcity.
In December 2023, students from Lincoln High School in Tulsa, Oklahoma, worked with the local city council to survey public transportation needs.
Professor Jonathan Edwards of the University of California stresses the importance of reflection, so students connect service activities with academic learning.
In January 2024, high school senior Sofia Rodriguez led a literacy campaign in El Paso, Texas, giving over 200 young children one-on-one reading support from student volunteers.

Sarah Thompson introduced a recycling initiative at her Boston middle school in February 2024; the note cites her as an example of teachers needing to back practical projects with solid academic content.
Service learning projects can require resources unavailable in all communities, creating disparities; advocacy groups have pushed for more funding for under-resourced schools.
"Project Future" was announced in March 2024 by a consortium of Midwestern universities to integrate service learning with career and technical education.
The "Global Classroom" project, begun in April 2024, uses video conferencing to connect students in New York with peers in Kenya on public health and sustainable development.
